messages:
Alex: Hey team  I finalized my divorce last week. Need to remove my ex-spouse from medical and set up COBRA for them. Divorce date was 35 days after the separation event and I missed the 30-day window. Can we still process the removal and COBRA start date?
Marin (People Ops): Sorry to hear that, Alex. Divorce is a qualifying life event—removals are allowed. For COBRA, we usually notify the carrier and the ex-spouse directly. The 30-day enrollment window applies to adding dependents; removals and COBRA notices have slightly different timelines but we still need the court decree.
Alex: OK. I have the signed decree but the court clerk added a processing stamp dated 20 days later. Does that matter?
Priya (Benefits): We'll need the final decree PDF. If the effective date on the decree shows the divorce date, we can use that as the event date. The clerk stamp is fine; if carrier asks for clarification we'll provide a cover letter.
Alex: Will I get a premium refund for the month after the decree? We paid premiums covering the spouse for the whole month and they had no claims.
Priya (Benefits): Refunds depend on the carrier and payroll cutoffs. If removal is processed retroactively to the decree date, carriers sometimes prorate premiums or issue refunds. Payroll may also need to reverse deductions. We'll coordinate benefits + payroll.
Alex: How will COBRA be handled for the ex? Do I need to give them contact info?
Marin (People Ops): We don't share your personal contact. We request the ex-spouse's mailing address and email so the carrier/COBRA administrator can send election notices. If you prefer we can ask them to contact benefits@redwood.com with ID info.
Alex: They live in another state. Anything special for out-of-state COBRA notices?
Priya (Benefits): COBRA is federal but state mini-COBRA rules vary. Our COBRA vendor handles out-of-state notices. Provide full mailing address, last known email, and date of loss of coverage (we'll confirm).
HRBot: Case created: BEN-1796789012. Please upload court decree to the benefits portal and email confirmation to benefits@redwood.com with subject BEN-EXPIRE-1796789012.
Marin (People Ops): Action items: 1) Upload signed court decree and any settlement docs. 2) Provide ex-spouse contact (mailing address + email). 3) If you want us to request a premium refund note that in the upload. We'll submit to carrier and payroll same day.
Alex: Uploading decree now and adding the ex-spouse address. Noting refund request. Thanks for the help.
Priya (Benefits): We'll escalate to the COBRA vendor and payroll. Expect initial confirmation in 3-7 business days; COBRA election packet to the ex-spouse within 14 days of our submission.
Marin (People Ops): Closing loop: we'll post updates here once COBRA vendor confirms mailing and payroll processes any refund. Reach out if you need help drafting the ex-spouse notice or blanking sensitive data.
Alex: Appreciate it, team.
